items.title: Three Mozambicans repatriated after being victims of human trafficking
items.summary: Maputo, 13 Oct (AIM) – The Mozambican government has announced the repatriation of three nationals who were victims of human trafficking in the Central African Republic. In a statement, the Ministry of Foreign Affairs explains that these individuals’ return follows several weeks of consultations and coordination among Mozambican authorities, the International Organization for Migration (IOM), and the government of the Central African Republic. “They all ensured the identification, protection, and safe return of the citizens. The citizens are now in their home region, central province of Manica province, since Thursday, October 8”, reads the note. The three Mozambicans are part of an initial group of 14 people. Of that total, seven returned to the country on their own, while four remain missing.

items.title: Germany's China calculation shifts as import pressures eclipse export benefits
items.summary: Germany long resisted tougher action against China because of retaliation fears. But rising pressure on key industries has pushed Berlin and Paris to seek stronger EU trade-defense powers to protect its industrial base Germany's cautious approach toward Beijing is cracking. items.title: Dozens of gold prospectors killed in strikes on Egypt-Sudan border, rights group says
items.summary: File photo of gold prospectors in northern Sudan At least 72 civilians who had been prospecting for gold in a border region of Sudan have been killed in air strikes, a regional rights group says Emergency Lawyers, based in the Sudanese capital, Khartoum, said jets targeted the so-called artisanal miners at a popular gold mining site in Red Sea state on Saturday Neither the Egyptian government nor the de facto Sudanese authorities have so far commented Cairo has previously faced accusations of deadly strikes on gold prospectors as part of a crackdown on illicit activity along its southern border Emergency Lawyers noted the previous alleged attacks and said they represented not only a violation of Sudan's sovereign territory but demonstrated the government's lack of control over the region "The deliberate targeting of unarmed civilians violates international humanitarian law and the right to life," it said in a statement on Sunday.
